outcome: severe morbidity (blood transfusion, surgical interventions, admission to intensive care unit)
cohort: The study included 312,151 women with objectively measured blood loss or other clinical markers of haemodynamic instability, participating in studies of postpartum haemorrhage.
finding: A decision rule combining measured blood loss (below the conventional threshold, e.g., 300mL or more) with any abnormal haemodynamic sign (pulse rate >100 bpm, SBP <100 mmHg, DBP <60 mmHg, or shock index >1.0) significantly improved prognostic accuracy for maternal mortality or severe morbidity.
